extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent practitioners, Patent Office officials, and courts handling patent matters
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules from the 1870 U.S. Patent Act setting forth requirements for patentability, application content and procedure, office practice (drawings, models, caveats, markings), priority/interference procedures, appeals, and related administrative powers and duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: All patents hereafter granted shall remain in force for the term of seventeen years from the date of issue; and all extension of such patents is hereby prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeatedly referenced: patents expire after 17 years; foreign-aligned patents may expire at same time as foreign patent but in no case shall be in force more than seventeen years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent formality — issuance and authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: All patents shall be issued in the name of the United States of America, under the seal of the Patent Office, and shall be signed by the Secretary of the Interior and countersigned by the commissioner, and they shall be recorded, together with the specification, in said office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner shall cause a seal to be provided; printed/certified copies of letters-patent with the seal and certification shall be legal evidence of the contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short title and annexed specification/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall contain a short title or description of the invention or discovery, correctly indicating its nature and design ... and a copy of said specifications and of the drawings shall be annexed to the patent and be a part thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short title must correctly indicate nature/design; drawings and specifications are part of the patent document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent dating and final fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall date as of a day not later than six months from the time at which it was passed and allowed, and notice thereof was sent to the applicant or his agent; and if the final fee shall not be paid within that period, the patent shall be withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final fee not timely paid the patent may be withheld; earlier act also provided that failure to pay within six months could render the invention public property as against the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive patentability requirements (novelty/utility/non-publication/prior_on-sale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has invented or discovered any new and useful art, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement thereof, not known or used by others in this country, and not patented, or described in any printed publication in this or any foreign country, before his invention or discovery thereof, and not in public use or on sale for more than two years prior to his application ... may obtain a patent therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires novelty (not known/used in US), no prior patent or printed publication anywhere, and not in public use/on sale in US for more than two years before application (unless proved abandoned). Also requires utility ('useful').

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign patent / prior foreign filing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall be debarred from receiving a patent by reason of its having been first patented or caused to be patented in a foreign country: Provided, The same shall not have been introduced into public use in the United States for more than two years prior to the application, and that the patent shall expire at the same time with the foreign patent ... but in no case shall it be in force more than seventeen years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign-first patents allowed subject to U.S. public-use/on-sale two-year bar and overall 17-year maximum term; patent term may be coextensive with foreign patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written application and specification content (enablement / best mode / distinct claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any inventor shall receive a patent he shall make application ... and shall file in the Patent Office a written description of the same, and of the manner and process of making, constructing, compounding, and using it, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art ... to make, construct, compound, and use the same; and in case of a machine, he shall explain the principle thereof, and the best mode in which he has contemplated applying that principle ... and he shall particularly point out and distinctly claim the part, improvement, or combination which he claims as his invention or discovery; and said specification and claim shall be signed by the inventor and attested by two witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains classic enablement, best mode, and distinct-claim requirements; specification and claims must be signed and witnessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings requirement and attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the nature of the case admits of drawings, the applicant shall furnish one copy signed by the inventor or his attorney in fact, and attested by two witnesses, which shall be filed in the Patent Office; and a copy of said drawings, to be furnished by the Patent Office, shall be attached to the patent as part of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant supplies signed/attested drawing(s); office attaches copy to patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens for compositions of matter
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention or discovery is of a composition of matter, the applicant, if required by the commissioner, shall furnish specimens of ingredients and of the composition, sufficient in quantity for the purpose of experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner has discretion to require material samples to permit experimental verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models when representation admits
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases which admit of representation by model, the applicant, if required by the commissioner, shall furnish one of convenient size to exhibit advantageously the several parts of his invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner may require a model to illustrate the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath of original inventor and citizenship statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall make oath or affirmation that he does verily believe himself to be the original and first inventor or discoverer ... that he does not know and does not believe that the same was ever before known or used; and shall state of what country he is a citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath may be made before authorized U.S. officers or certain foreign officials or notaries when applicant resides abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to cause examination and standard for issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: On the filing of any such application and the payment of the duty required by law, the commissioner shall cause an examination to be made of the alleged new invention or discovery; and if ... it shall appear that the claimant is justly entitled to a patent under the law, and that the same is sufficiently useful and important, the commissioner shall issue a patent therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner carries out substantive examination for entitlement and utility/importance before issuing patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution timeline and abandonment rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications for patents shall be completed and prepared for examination within two years after the filing of the petition, and in default thereof, or upon failure of the applicant to prosecute the same within two years after any action therein, of which notice shall have been given to the applicant, they shall be regarded as abandoned ... unless it be shown to the satisfaction of the commissioner that such delay was unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-year prosecution clock; commissioner discretion to excuse unavoidable delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and who must apply/sworn specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be granted and issued or reissued to the assignee of the inventor or discoverer, the assignment thereof being first entered of record in the Patent Office; but in such case the application for the patent shall be made and the specification sworn to by the inventor or discoverer; and also, if he be living, in case of an application for reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignee can be grantee only if assignment recorded; inventor must still make/sign the application and oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights when inventor dies before patent (representative applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: When any person having made any new invention dies before a patent is granted, the right of applying for and obtaining the patent shall devolve on his executor or administrator, in trust for the heirs at law ... and when the application shall be made by such legal representatives, the oath or affirmation required to be made shall be so varied in form that it can be made by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal representatives may prosecute applications on behalf of deceased inventors with adapted oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to apply after failure to pay final fee or prior allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person having an interest in an invention for which a patent was ordered to issue upon the payment of the final fee, but who has failed to make payment thereof within six months from the time at which it was passed and allowed ... shall have a right to make an application for a patent for such invention ... Provided, That the second application be made within two years after the allowance of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a second-chance application window for certain failure-to-pay situations; earlier acts also allowed payment within six months to receive withheld patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal window for rejected or withdrawn applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application for a patent has been rejected or withdrawn, prior to the passage of this act, the applicant shall have six months from the date of such passage to renew his application, or to file a new one; and if he omit to do either, his application shall be held to have been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment treated as question of fact upon hearing of renewed applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation of assignments to protect against subsequent purchasers/mortgagees
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent or any interest therein shall be assignable in law, by an instrument in writing; ... said assignment, grant, or conveyance shall be void as against any subsequent purchaser or mortgagee for a valuable consideration, without notice, unless it is recorded in the Patent Office within three months from the date thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-month recording window to preserve priority of assignment against bona fide purchasers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-user defense for specific constructive acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who may have purchased of the inventor, or with his knowledge and consent may have constructed any newly invented ... machine, or other patentable article, prior to the application by the inventor ... shall have the right to use, and vend to others to be used, the specific thing so made or purchased, without liability therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects prior purchasers/users who acted with inventor's knowledge before inventor filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement and consequences of marking patented articles
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be the duty of all patentees ... and of all persons making or vending any patented article for or under them, to give sufficient notice to the public that the same is patented, either by fixing thereon the word 'patented,' together with the day and year the patent was granted; ... and in any suit for infringement, by the party failing so to mark, no damages shall be recovered by the plaintiff, except on proof that the defendant was duly notified of the infringement, and continued, after such notice, to make, use, or vend the article so patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper marking required to recover damages absent actual notice; alternative labelling of package allowed when marking on article not practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for false marking / counterfeit patent marking
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person shall ... mark upon any thing made, used, or sold by him for which he has not obtained a patent ... the word 'patent' ... for the purpose of deceiving the public, he shall be liable ... to a penalty of not less than one hundred dollars, with costs; one moiety of said penalty to the person who shall sue for the same, and the other to the use of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False marking is a statutory offense with minimum penalty and qui tam-like distribution of proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any citizen who desires further time to mature an invention may file a caveat setting forth the design thereof, and of its distinguishing characteristics, and praying protection of his right until he shall have matured his invention; such caveat shall be filed in the confidential archives ... and shall be operative for the term of one year ... if application made within the year by any other person that would interfere, the commissioner shall deposit the description/specifications/drawings/model of such application ... and give notice to the person filing the caveat, who shall file his description, specifications, drawings, and model within three months from the time of placing said notice in the post-office in Washington ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat provides one-year confidential priority-protecting window and triggers notice and limited response time if conflicting application is filed; aliens may file under residency/intention conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection notice and information to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, on examination, any claim for a patent is rejected for any reason whatever, the commissioner shall notify the applicant thereof, giving him briefly the reasons for such rejection, together with such information and references as may be useful in judging of the propriety of renewing his application or of altering his specification; and if ... the applicant shall persist in his claim ... the commissioner shall order a re-examination of the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner must provide brief reasons and useful references when rejecting claims; applicant can prompt re-examination by persisting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference/priority practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an application is made which would interfere with any pending application, or with any unexpired patent, the commissioner shall give notice ... and shall direct the primary examiner to proceed to determine the question of priority of invention. And the commissioner may issue a patent to the party adjudged the prior inventor, unless the adverse party shall appeal ... within such time, not less than twenty days, as the commissioner shall prescribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies notice, primary-examiner determination of priority, and short appeal window (not less than 20 days) to challenge priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for affidavits and depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioner may establish rules for taking affidavits and depositions required in cases pending in the Patent Office, and such affidavits and depositions may be taken before any officer authorized by law to take depositions to be used in the courts of the United States, or of the State where the officer resides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner sets procedures for testimonial evidence used in PTO proceedings; such testimony is admissible in courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena power for testimony in contested Patent Office cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The clerk of any court of the United States ... wherein testimony is to be taken for use in any contested case pending in the Patent Office, shall, upon application ... issue a subpoena for any witness residing or being within said district or territory, commanding him to appear and testify ... and if any witness ... shall neglect or refuse to appear ... the judge ... may enforce obedience to the process, or punish the disobedience as in other like cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court clerks can issue subpoenas for Patent Office contested cases; judges can enforce obedience or punish contempt, subject to fee/travel conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness fees and attendance limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Every witness duly subpoenaed and in attendance shall be allowed the same fees as are allowed to witnesses attending the courts of the United States, but no witness shall be required to attend at any place more than forty miles from the place where the subpoena is served ... nor be deemed guilty of contempt ... unless his fees and travelling expenses ... are paid or tendered him at the time of the service of the subpoena; nor for refusing to disclose any secret invention or discovery made or owned by himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects witnesses from excessive travel and ensures fees/t expenses are tendered; allows refusal to disclose own secret invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights within Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Every applicant for a patent or the reissue of a patent, any of the claims of which have been twice rejected, and every party to an interference, may appeal from the decision of the primary examiner ... to the board of examiners-in-chief, having once paid the fee for such appeal provided by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes internal appeal to board of examiners-in-chief after two rejections or in interferences, subject to fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further appeals — to commissioner and court
rubrics_metrics.description: If such party is dissatisfied with the decision of the examiners-in-chief, he may, on payment of the duty required by law, appeal to the commissioner in person. If ... dissatisfied with the decision of the commissioner, he may appeal to the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia, sitting in banc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets sequential appellate path: primary examiner → board of examiners-in-chief → commissioner → Supreme Court of D.C.; subject to fees/duties and (for interference parties) certain limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for taking appeal to court (notice and reasons)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appeal is taken to the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia, the appellant shall give notice thereof to the commissioner, and file in the Patent Office, within such time as the commissioner shall appoint, his reasons of appeal, specifically set forth in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must notify commissioner and file written, specific reasons within appointed time; court's revision confined to points set forth in reasons of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's summary revision duty and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be the duty of said court, on petition, to hear and determine such appeal and to revise the decision appealed from in a summary way, on the evidence produced before the commissioner ... and after hearing the case, the court shall return to the commissioner a certificate of its proceedings and decision, which shall be entered of record in the Patent Office, and govern the further proceedings in the case. But no opinion or decision of the court in any such case shall preclude any person interested from the right to contest the validity of such patent in any court wherein the same may be called in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court proceedings are summary and confined to specified points; the court's certificate governs further PTO proceedings but does not bar other validity challenges in other courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners-in-chief qualifications and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiners-in-chief shall be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability, whose duty it shall be, on the written petition of the appellant, to revise and determine upon the validity of the adverse decisions of examiners upon applications for patents, and for reissues of patents, and in interference cases; and when required by the commissioner, they shall hear and report upon claims for extensions, and perform such other like duties as he may assign them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies required mix of legal and scientific competence and enumerates appellate and interference responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner powers over office practice and filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioner may ... require all papers filed in the Patent Office, if not correctly, legibly and clearly written, to be printed at the cost of the party filing them. The commissioner, subject to approval of the Secretary, may from time to time establish rules and regulations, not inconsistent with law, for the conduct of proceedings in the Patent Office. The commissioner may print copies of specifications and drawings and copies of claims of current issues and necessary laws/decisions/rules/circulars for public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner has broad administrative authority to order printing, promulgate rules, and publish official materials; subject to Secretary approval where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner duties regarding custody, public inspection, and disposition of models and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioner shall have charge of all books, records, papers, models, machines, and other things belonging to said office ... shall cause to be classified and arranged ... the models, specimens ... deposited in said office; and said rooms and galleries shall be kept open during suitable hours for public inspection. The commissioner may restore to applicants models of rejected applications he deems unnecessary to preserve, or may sell or otherwise dispose of them after the application has been finally rejected for one year, paying the proceeds into the treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner oversees preservation, classification, and limited public access to deposited materials; has discretion to return or dispose of unneeded models after one year post-final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Patent Office employees acquiring patent interests
rubrics_metrics.description: All officers and employees of the Patent Office shall be incapable, during the period for which they shall hold their appointments, to acquire or take, directly or indirectly, except by inheritance or bequest, any right or interest in any patent issued by said office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents conflicts of interest by forbidding acquisition of patent interests during tenure (except by inheritance/bequest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing/certified copies and their evidentiary value
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed copies of the letters-patent of the United States, with the seal of the Patent Office affixed thereto and certified and signed by the Commissioner of Patents, shall be legal evidence of the contents of said letters-patent in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified printed copies serve as legal evidence; commissioner authorized to print copies of specifications, claims, drawings and related laws/decisions for public information, with specified cost limits in earlier provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and procedure when an application would interfere with pending application or patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an application is made for a patent which, in the opinion of the commissioner, would interfere with any pending application, or with any unexpired patent, he shall give notice thereof to the applicants ... and shall direct the primary examiner to proceed to determine the question of priority of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner must notify affected parties and direct primary examiner to resolve priority; parties may appeal within time prescribed.
